1.why: All nine screens are static, flat cards with no animations, carousels, or pop-up overlays; the only extra panel is a fixed 'Need help?' sidebar.

2.why: Headings are large and bold, primary actions are solid dark-blue filled buttons versus outlined secondary ones, and 'Next:' callouts are highlighted, though the always-visible Logs box competes slightly for attention.

3.why: Each screen shows only one task with a single input field and a clearly dominant primary button, plus a persistent help link in the header, making the needed element easy to locate.

4.why: A four-segment progress bar, explicit 'Step 1/2/3' labels, 'Next:' previews, and on-screen password rules offload most memory demands, though she must still carry the long recovery code from the log into the field.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password-manager hint, autofill affordance, or show-password toggle appears on any of the sign-in or password screens.

6.why: Consistent layout aids familiarity, but nothing personal is recognizable — no saved email/username, masked account hint, or previously used device shown; the email field is always blank.

7.why: Sentences are short, plain-language and one idea each (e.g. 'Step 1: Tell us the email address or patient reference connected to your account.'), with password rules as a three-item bullet list.

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the nine screenshots, so the claim that error messages explain the problem and the fix cannot be observed as true of this system.

9.why: The password screen lists requirements but gives no example password, and the email/patient-reference and code fields have no placeholder or sample format shown.

10.why: The offered options (password sign-in, 'Forgot password?', recovery code, verification code, 'Pause and return later') are clearly labelled, but only password-based routes exist — no face/biometric or alternative login choice is presented.

11.why: Every screen presents at most one primary and one secondary action plus one help link, avoiding simultaneous choice overload.

12.why: Confirmation screens ('Privacy conditions accepted', 'You have completed this task'), 'Next:' statements, and the simulated log lines report what happened after each action, though the log wording is technical.

13.why: A persistent 'Need help?' panel, 'Help and safe advice' link, 'Read safe recovery advice' link, and per-step 'Next:' tips provide short guidance for each new step.

14.why: 'Back to sign in', 'Return to sign in', and 'Pause and return later' allow re-entry, but no explicit retry/resend-code affordance or recoverable error path is visible.

15.why: All nine screens reuse the identical header, card layout, typography, button styling, help sidebar, and log panel position.
